$comment: Round 1 review (renderer hardening): interaction semantics every renderer must share, HAND-AUTHORED and replayed by packages/exponential-ui-react/src/interactions-fixture.test.tsx (the reference, jsdom) and apps/desktop/crates/eui-core/tests/interactions_fixture.rs (the core, so gpui and the natives through the FFI). numberField: a NumberField bound to /v (value null = /v unseeded), one op (increment / decrement press, commit = type `input` then leave the field, none), then the value at /v and the text the field shows (en-US; `precision` absent = the step's decimals; values round like toFixed, the text like Intl.NumberFormat with that many fraction digits; a stepper on an unset value starts from min when min > 0, else 0; a stepper at its limit is disabled). checks: a Form `f` holding Checkbox `agree` (checked bound to /agreed) with `checks` and a submit Button; submitting gives the failing messages in order (a check WITH a condition fails when it resolves to nothing, null, false or an empty string; 0 passes; a non-string message reads `Invalid value`) and whether `submit` fired. tableSort: an UNBOUND sort of literal rows by one column (`sortRows`: missing values last both ways, two numbers numerically, a number column coerces, a date column by time, booleans as 0/1, the rest by Intl.Collator(locale, {numeric: true, sensitivity: base}); ties keep row order) → the row indexes in display order. choiceTiles (EXP-1280): a ChoiceTiles `c` over options a, b, c (`disabled` = the index of a disabled option) with `value` bound to /v (null = unseeded), the tiles pressed in order (a press on any part of tile i), then /v and every `change` value fired: single picks the pressed value; multiple toggles it in the comma-joined list kept in OPTION order (nothing picked = an empty string); a disabled option does nothing. select (VAPP-146): a plain single Select `s` over the options Any (value ""), Open (open) and Done (done) with `value` bound to /v (null = unseeded), the options picked in order (open the trigger, press option i), then /v, the text the trigger shows and every `change` value fired: an empty string is an ordinary option value (never refused, never the error placeholder); an unseeded value reads as "", so the trigger shows the option holding ""; picking an option writes its value; picking the option that holds the current value fires nothing (the empty one included, an unseeded /v stays unseeded). buttonHold (VAPP-162, docs/round-5-contract.md §9): a Button `b` (label `Hold to talk`, `holdingLabel` `Holding…` unless the case says otherwise) laid out at 120 × 40 px, coordinates relative to its top-left; `props` override the button's (null = unset; the base props are `hold: true`); `steps` = pointerdown/pointermove/pointerup at {x, y}, pointercancel, keydown/keyup {key}, blur; after each step `events` = the events that step fired (in order) and `pressed` / `label` = what the button paints. THE RULE: with `hold: true` a press never fires `press`; pointer down (or Space/Enter key down; key repeat ignored) fires `holdStart` and paints the pressed state + `holdingLabel`; while the hold is active the pointer may wander up to 24 px (the slop) outside the box; release (pointer up anywhere within the slop, or key up of the key that started it) fires `holdEnd`; the pointer leaving the box by more than the slop (the slide away), pointercancel, Escape or losing focus fire `holdCancel`; after a cancel nothing fires until the next down. `disabled` fires nothing; `hold: false` keeps the plain `press` on release over the box. VAPP-206 rowPress: a Table bound to /rows whose on.rowPress action reads {path: <value>} (a set's value, an event's context); pressing row `press` reads `expect`: the action's relative paths read the pressed row, absolute ones the data model. VAPP-279 tabsReorder: the six-tab strip of fixtures/tabs-strip.json `layout` (fifth active, closable on hover, addable, theme default, fixed measure) at 900 px in `direction`; `tab` = the tab index the steps act on. `drag {phase, delta}` = what a painter sends for a pointer (or touch long-press) drag, delta = px since the start in screen direction; `order` = the tab values in strip order after the step (the live preview); the end drops the preview and fires `reorder {from, to, value}` when the tab changed place (array indexes; the host owns `tabs`). `key` = what a painter sends for Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+ArrowLeft/ArrowRight on the tab. `expect` = every `reorder` fired, in order. #VAPP-284 foldRow (docs/round-7-contract.md): the tree = `surface` (a Row `issues` with two child Rows, `open` bound to /open, on.press = event `select`, on.change = event `fold`; `pressable: false` drops on.press, so the head itself folds); /open starts at `open`; `rtl` puts the Row in a `direction: rtl` box; ONE step: `press` the part (`head` = `issues.head`, `fold` = `issues.head.fold`) or `key` (a DOM key name) on it while focused; then `events` = the event names fired in order and `after` = /open. THE RULE: a pressable head presses as `select` and its fold button folds; a plain head folds; ArrowRight opens and ArrowLeft closes (swapped in rtl) the focused head or fold button, firing `fold` (context {open}) and writing /open; a key that would not change the state does nothing. #VAPP-285 tree (docs/round-7-contract.md): `surface` = a Tree `files` over the repository of fixtures/tree.json with `expanded` bound to /open and `value` to /picked (so every row is in the tree; `rowIds` maps an item id to its row node), on.select = event `open`, on.toggle = `fold`, on.load = `fetch`; /open starts at `open`, /picked unset; `rtl` puts the Tree in a `direction: rtl` box; ONE step: `press` the row of an item or `key` (a DOM key name) on it while focused; then `events` = the event names fired in order, `after.open` = /open, `after.picked` = /picked (null = unset), `after.focus` = the item whose row has the focus after a key (null = the focus did not move), `after.visible` (when given) = the visible rows' items in order. THE RULE: a leaf press selects (`open {id}`, /picked = id); a branch press folds (`fold {id, open}`, the id added to or removed from /open); a lazy branch (hasChildren, no children) folds through `fetch` and shows its loading row while open; the arrows follow treeKey over the VISIBLE rows (Down/Up, Home/End, Right opens a closed branch or enters an open one, Left closes an open branch or goes to the parent; swapped in rtl). fieldWrites (#VAPP-288): an Input `draft` (value bound to /draft, seeded `seed`) and a Button `save` whose press is `functionCall set {path, value}` (`press` sets `pressPath` to `pressValue`); steps: `focus`, `type` (the field's own edit: the text the person typed, written through to the data model like every edit), `hostWrite` (the host writes `value` at `path`: updateDataModel, a bind, a server's echo), `press` (the Button), `blur`; then the text the field shows and the value at /draft. THE ECHO RULE stays for everything that is not a programmatic write: a focused field (or one with an edit outstanding) keeps its text against a host write. A PROGRAMMATIC write (an action's `set` step: a press's `functionCall set`, a package action's `sets`) bumps the surface's write epoch; a field whose bound value changed since it last looked AND saw the epoch move adopts the new value even while focused (the cursor at the end, an outstanding edit dropped). A programmatic write to another path leaves the field alone. Round 8 checkbox (docs/round-8-contract.md §2): the tree = `surface` (a Checkbox `c` with `checked` bound to /checked and `indeterminate` bound to /mixed, on.change = event `change`); `data` seeds /checked and /mixed (absent = unseeded), `unbound` (when given) replaces the two bindings with those LITERAL props; then `presses` presses on the box (`c.box`); `before` = the checked state painters expose before any press (`mixed` | `true` | `false`: mixed wins over checked; the box paints the checked look with the dash `Checkbox.check.indeterminate`); after each press `steps[i]` = {change: the change event's context {checked, indeterminate}, checked: /checked, mixed: /mixed (null = unseeded; for an unbound case the box's own props), state}. THE RULE: a press on a mixed box sets checked TRUE and indeterminate false (both written: bound paths through their bindings), whatever checked was; a press on a plain box toggles checked and writes nothing to indeterminate (an unseeded /mixed stays unseeded); `change` always carries {checked, indeterminate: false}. checkSeverities (round 9 §6.6): a Form `f` holding Input `x` (name x, validateOn submit) with `checks` over data results and a submit Button `go`; after pressing `go`: `submitted`, the `errors` of `invalid`, and the ONE message `shown`: part `x.error` holds it, in recipe state `invalid` for an error, `warning` / `info` otherwise (role alert / status on web); `invalid` = the Input's own `invalid` state. Only a failing error blocks. buttonChecks: a Button `b` with `checks` and a `press` action: a failing error disables it, warning and info never do; `disabled` = the press does not fire. boxHover (#EDE-65): a Box's `on.hover` fires when the pointer ENTERS it, exactly like Motion's: no payload (the action's own context only), leaving fires nothing, entering again fires again; a Box need not be pressable to hover, and a pressable one still presses. The tree = `surface` (Boxes `a` and `b` with on.hover = event `hovered` {id}, `b` also pressable with on.press = `pressed`, `c` without on.hover); `steps` = `enter` / `leave` / `press` on a Box by id; `events` = the actions fired, in order, {name, context}. tilePress (#FEED-201): StatTile and Card fire `press` like a pressable Box (an `on.press` implies `pressable`: a button, the Row hover fill); a StatTile's press target is its card part (`<id>.card`), a Card's its root; a Card without `on.press` stays a group and fires nothing. Same shape as boxHover (`press` steps only). overlayAnchor (#EXP-1739): an open anchored overlay (Popover, Menu, Tooltip) CLOSES once its anchor scrolls (a scroll container holding it scrolls), moves (its box's origin changes: here a node inserted above it) or leaves the tree; a frame that moves nothing keeps it. `surface` is a scrolling Stack holding the anchor `target` and a Popover open against it; a step re-lays out (`relayout`), scrolls `list` by `y`, inserts `above` before the anchor (`insertAbove`) or drops the anchor (`removeAnchor`); `after` = whether the Popover is still open. keyRecorder (#EXP-1629): KeyRecorder is a macro (a Box `field` + Kbd caps); the renderers capture, the HOST owns the grammar. `surface` = a KeyRecorder `ptt` with value, pending and recording bound (/value, /pending, /recording unseeded), on.start = `pause`, on.stop = `resume`, on.key = `key`. Steps: `press` the field (a click, or Enter/Space while idle), `down`/`up` a key with the `mods` held, `modifiers` = the held set changes to these (a modifier key alone: the platform's own modifier-change event), `mouse` = button n pressed over the field (1 left, 2 right, 3 middle, 4 back, 5 forward), `blur` = the field loses focus, `hostWrite` = the host writes `value` at `path`; then `events` = the actions fired in order {name, context} and `recording` = /recording (null = unset). THE RULE: a press while idle fires `start` and writes recording true (the two-way set), and the field takes the focus; a press while recording does nothing. While recording (the field's `recording` recipe prop, read live) EVERY key goes to `key` and nothing else sees it (no Tab focus move, no Escape dismiss, no shortcut, no key repeat): a non-modifier key down/up = {type: down|up, key}, a modifier key alone = {type: modifiers}, mouse buttons 3-5 over the field = {type: mouse, button} (1 and 2 fire nothing), each with the held flags {ctrl, alt, shift, meta} (meta = Cmd / Super / Win). `key` is the CANONICAL name, the same on every platform: a-z, 0-9 (the physical key, never the shifted character), f1-f24, space, enter, tab, escape, backspace, delete, insert, home, end, pageup, pagedown, up, down, left, right, and the US-layout punctuation of the key (- = [ ] \ ; ' , . / `); a key outside that list is not sent. Losing the focus while recording fires `stop` and writes recording false. The host stops recording by writing recording false (no `stop` fires); idle, keys and blur fire nothing. composerKeys (#EDE-65): `menuKeys` lets a host drive a suggestion menu above a Composer by keyboard (eDE's `/` menu, the @ / # / : typeahead); the host moves its own highlighted row. The tree = `surface` (a Composer `c` with value bound to /draft and menuKeys bound to /menu, on.submit = event `send`, on.key = event `key`); `data` seeds /draft and /menu. Steps: `type` = the field's own edit (the text written through to /draft), `key` = a key down in the field (SearchList's DOM-style names, the catalog's one key naming: ArrowUp, ArrowDown, Enter, Tab, Escape) with the `mods` held (ctrl, alt, shift, meta) and `composing` = an IME composition is in progress, `hostWrite` = the host writes `value` at `path`; `handled` on a key step = the Composer took the key (the field does not edit, move its caret, submit or move the focus, and nothing outside sees it). Then `events` = the actions fired in order {name, context} and `draft` = /draft (null = unset). THE RULE: while menuKeys is true (read live), Up, Down, Enter, Tab and Escape with NO modifier held fire `key` {key} (that same name: ArrowUp, ArrowDown, Enter, Tab, Escape) and nothing else (Enter never submits, busy or not); a key with any modifier held (Shift+Enter's newline, Shift+Tab, Alt+Down) is never intercepted, and every key during an IME composition is the IME's (never `key`, never a submit, menuKeys on or off). While menuKeys is false nothing changes: Enter submits (`submit` {value: the trimmed text}, the draft cleared; an empty draft submits nothing), Shift+Enter is the field's newline, the arrows, Tab and Escape are the field's own. composerSlots (#EDE-65 R): a Composer's `leading` and `trailing` slots hold any genUI child, drawn INSIDE the composer's controls row (the send disc's row at the bottom of its content box). Each case = a Composer `c` with the case's `props` and `slots` (in `direction`, default ltr) inside a 400 px wide surface; `order` = the row's controls from the START edge (`leading`, `attachment` = the attach control when `attachments`, `trailing`, `send`). THE RULE: `leading` starts at the content box's start edge; a spacer takes the free width; `trailing` ends one row gap (`$spacing.xs`) before the send disc; the attach control ends one gap before `trailing` (before the disc without it), so without slots nothing moves; every slot root is vertically centred on the disc and inside the composer's box; the field above is unchanged (slots never size the composer). #EXP-1762 `layout: "flat"`: ONE row, the field (`field` in `order`) takes the spacer's place, between `leading` and the attach control (or `trailing`, or the disc), one row gap either side; the controls stay in the bottom row (vertically centred on the disc) while the field grows upward; the field box SPANS the row (its top = the content box's top, its height = the row's: the disc's while the draft is one line) and the text's first line starts the Composer `field` recipe's `paddingTop` below the field box's top, one line or grown alike (the app's bottom-aligned row: neutral `$spacing.sm` = (disc 36 − line 20) / 2, the exponential theme 4.25, the IDE's); the row grows past the disc once paddingTop + the text's lines (+ any paddingBottom) are taller; the field wraps at the width the slots and controls leave. A case's `data` seeds the surface (the draft at /draft); `field` = the geometry check {rows: the draft's lines, grown: whether the row is taller than the disc}: the field box's top and height are the row's, the text's top = field top + paddingTop (a renderer without layout, jsdom, checks the field's resolved padding-top is the recipe's and that it stretches across the row). A slot child is a real node: `press` = press the node with that id; `events` = the actions fired in order {name, context}. composerPaste (#EDE-65 R): pasting into a Composer's field (`attachments` on or off). `clipboard` = what the paste carries: `text` and `files` [{name, size, type}]. THE RULE: when the paste carries image files (`type` image/*), the Composer fires the existing `attach` event with context {files: [{name, size, type}]} (only the images, in clipboard order; the same file shape as FileUpload's `upload`), hands their bytes to the host's upload hook (web `onUpload(files, {nodeId, name})`, gpui `on_upload`, SwiftUI / Compose `onUpload`; `name` = the Composer's id) and inserts nothing; a native clipboard image without a file name is `image.<ext of its type>` (`image.png`). A paste carrying files but no image does nothing (no `attach`, no text: a copied file's path is no draft); a paste without files is the field's own (the text inserted, `change` fired, no `attach`). The attach control's press still fires `attach` with no context. Then `events` = the actions fired in order and `draft` = /draft. pickerPick (#EXP-1760): IconPicker and ColorPicker are macros over a Popover; `surface` = which of `surfaces`, `data` = the seeded model. Steps: `press` = press the node with that id (`<id>.trigger` opens, a ColorPicker with a child opens on `<id>.customTrigger` (a ghost button around it), `<id>.scroll.grid.cell.<i>` / `<id>.grid.swatch.<i>` / `<id>.none` pick; an `inline` ColorPicker is the grid alone: `<id>.swatch.<i>` picks, there is no popover, so `open` stays false). THE RULE: a pick sets the bound `value` (the cell's icon, the swatch's hex, `""` for No icon), fires the author's `change` with context {value} and CLOSES the popover (`open: false`); the trigger only opens it and fires nothing; the Popover's own open/close never fires the author's `change` (the cells claim it). Then `events` = the actions fired in order, `value` = /value, `open` = whether the popover shows.
